articles.description:
🚀 Introduction
In this blog post, you'll learn:
What is hoisting in JavaScript?
How variables and functions are hoisted
The difference between var, let, and const
Real examples and a mental model to remember hoisting
🔍 What is Hoisting?
This means you can use variables and functions before you declare them — but there’s a catch!
📌 Example 1: Variable Hoisting with var
console.log(name); // undefined
var name = "Ankur";


Explanation:
name is hoisted, but only the declaration (not the value) is moved to the top.It’s as if you wrote:
var name;
console.log(name); // undefined
name = "Ankur";


🚫 What about let and const?
console.log(age); // ❌ ReferenceError
let age = 25;


Variables declared with letand const are not initialized during hoisting.
📌 Example 2: Function Hoisting
greet();

function greet() {
  console.log("Hello there!");
}


✅ This works!
⚠️ Function Expressions are NOT Hoisted
sayHi(); // ❌ TypeError

var sayHi = function () {
  console.log("Hi!");
};


🧠 Visual Model of Hoisting

📝 Summary



Concept
Hoisted?
Accessible before declaration?




var
✅ Yes
⚠️ Yes, but value is undefined



let / const

✅ Yes
❌ No, in TDZ


Function Declaration
✅ Yes
✅ Yes


Function Expression
❌ No
❌ No



💬 Final Thoughts
🔗 Read Full Blog with Code and Visuals
https://webcodingwithankur.blogspot.com/2025/06/what-is-hoisting-in-javascript.html

articles.description:
API Gateways and Service Meshes both deal with service communication and traffic control, but they operate in different parts of the architecture and solve distinct problems. Understanding their differences helps in choosing the right tool or knowing when to use both together. Let’s break it down by key aspects:

API Gateway: It manages north-south traffic, i.e., communication between external clients and internal services by acting as the entry point for all inbound API requests.
Service Mesh: They handle east-west traffic, which refers to service-to-service communication inside the application network. It ensures reliable and secure connections between internal microservices.
API Gateway: Sits at the edge of the network, intercepting and managing all external requests before they reach b…
